A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

evidence.content_invariant: Each file contains only Lake DSL package, require and lean_lib commands; no theorem, definition, statement, proof, or mathematical interface. All theorem-bearing modules they build stay retained.
evidence.rationale: These exact files are Lake build configuration (package options, pinned dependencies, library targets) for the OpenGALib package and its Prove2Me submission sub-packages, not Riemannian-geometry formalization.
review_evidence: lakefile.lean: package OpenGALib with leanOptions, require mathlib @0df444a3 and DifferentialGeometry @1b535dd1, lean_lib OpenGALib roots/globs.

PoincareConjecture/lakefile.lean and Contributions/{BishopGromov,ComparisonGeometry,MeasuredSurgery,WidthAreaEvolution,Varifold,ExtinctionEndgame/Upload}/lakefile.lean: package block, require mathlib @0df444a3, lean_lib Definitions/Theorems/Solutions globs.
Contributions/{ClosedSurfaceArea,ImmersedSurfaceMetric,SurfaceArea}/lakefile.lean: same, plus lean_lib Verified globs.
Contributions/Drafts, Contributions/ExtinctionEndgame, References/ColdingMinicozzi lakefile.lean: package block, require OpenGALib from relative path, one lean_lib target with roots.

evidence.content_invariant: Each file contains only Lake DSL package, require and lean_lib commands; no theorem, definition, statement, proof, or mathematical interface. All theorem-bearing modules they build stay retained.
evidence.rationale: These exact files are Lake build configuration (package options, pinned dependencies, library targets) for the OpenGALib package and its Prove2Me submission sub-packages, not Riemannian-geometry formalization.
review_evidence: lakefile.lean: package OpenGALib with leanOptions, require mathlib @0df444a3 and DifferentialGeometry @1b535dd1, lean_lib OpenGALib roots/globs.

PoincareConjecture/lakefile.lean and Contributions/{BishopGromov,ComparisonGeometry,MeasuredSurgery,WidthAreaEvolution,Varifold,ExtinctionEndgame/Upload}/lakefile.lean: package block, require mathlib @0df444a3, lean_lib Definitions/Theorems/Solutions globs.
Contributions/{ClosedSurfaceArea,ImmersedSurfaceMetric,SurfaceArea}/lakefile.lean: same, plus lean_lib Verified globs.
Contributions/Drafts, Contributions/ExtinctionEndgame, References/ColdingMinicozzi lakefile.lean: package block, require OpenGALib from relative path, one lean_lib target with roots.

title: Repository-local audited exclusion

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

Restated from RRV-9fd1bd902e6b-r1: every selected file is byte-identical to the reviewed file.

justification: This file is excluded only because an accepted repository-review record targets its exact current content through an exact path, exact path set, or literal subtree prefix. The review record is pinned to the reviewed work-unit snapshot and records the repository-local rationale, content-level losslessness invariant, evidence, selector, and source provenance. FD-018 authorizes no filename, path role, generated directory, or cross-repository class by itself; any changed work-unit snapshot makes the review stale and blocks indexing until it is re-audited.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.

Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp: manually inspected; its 179 quote and 1 semicolon occurrences are all inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols such as (C$::|C17-CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|) and (C$::|C17-CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) naming C grammar terminals, and its head/tail match the same bare-symbol/fire-count-tuple format as the rest of the file and this unit's other .sys files.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp: manually inspected; its 179 quote and 1 semicolon occurrences are all inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols such as (C$::|C17-CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|) and (C$::|C17-CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) naming C grammar terminals, and its head/tail match the same bare-symbol/fire-count-tuple format as the rest of the file and this unit's other .sys files.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp: manually inspected; its 179 quote and 1 semicolon occurrences are all inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols such as (C$::|C17-CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|) and (C$::|C17-CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) naming C grammar terminals, and its head/tail match the same bare-symbol/fire-count-tuple format as the rest of the file and this unit's other .sys files.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
title: ACL2 useless-runes proof metadata retained

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp: manually inspected; its 179 quote and 1 semicolon occurrences are all inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols such as (C$::|C17-CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|) and (C$::|C17-CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) naming C grammar terminals, and its head/tail match the same bare-symbol/fire-count-tuple format as the rest of the file and this unit's other .sys files.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/abstract-syntax-trees@useless-runes.lsp (2253885 bytes, largest) and books/kestrel/c/syntax/tests/.sys/types-to-tynames@useless-runes.lsp (47 bytes, smallest): individually checked, same result.

The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 45 files individually scanned end to end (via full read for files under 300 lines, head/tail sampling for larger ones) with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0, and grep -c for '"' and ';' also returning 0, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format throughout with no declaration, string, or comment content.
books/kestrel/arm/.sys/instructions@useless-runes.lsp (17711 lines, largest): head/tail sampled, bare-symbol/tuple format confirmed.
books/kestrel/fty/.sys/map@useless-runes.lsp (1 line) and books/kestrel/fty/.sys/fty-treeset@useless-runes.lsp (11 lines): read in full, single/short bare-symbol lists confirmed.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp contains pipe-escaped symbol names for Rust lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|, |CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) whose embedded quote and semicolon characters a naive grep flags, but a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format as every other file in this rule, matching the pattern already established for a Java grammar file in an earlier unit.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 54 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format with no declaration content.

grep -c for '"' and ';' returned 0 for 53 of the 54 files; books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp returned 62 and 1 respectively, traced line-by-line to pipe-escaped grammar-terminal symbol names, with grep -n '^;' confirming zero true comment lines.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. In books/kestrel/java/language/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp the quote and semicolon characters found by a naive grep belong to pipe-escaped symbol names for Java lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|), not to string literals or comments; a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp contains pipe-escaped symbol names for Rust lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|, |CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) whose embedded quote and semicolon characters a naive grep flags, but a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format as every other file in this rule, matching the pattern already established for a Java grammar file in an earlier unit.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 54 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format with no declaration content.

grep -c for '"' and ';' returned 0 for 53 of the 54 files; books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp returned 62 and 1 respectively, traced line-by-line to pipe-escaped grammar-terminal symbol names, with grep -n '^;' confirming zero true comment lines.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. In books/kestrel/java/language/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp the quote and semicolon characters found by a naive grep belong to pipe-escaped symbol names for Java lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|), not to string literals or comments; a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 4 files individually scanned end to end (full read for the two under 50000 bytes, head/tail sampling plus targeted line-content checks for the two larger ones) with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format with no declaration content.
books/kestrel/java/language/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp: grep -n for lines starting with ';' returned no matches, ruling out comment content despite nonzero raw semicolon/quote character counts.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp contains pipe-escaped symbol names for Rust lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|, |CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) whose embedded quote and semicolon characters a naive grep flags, but a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format as every other file in this rule, matching the pattern already established for a Java grammar file in an earlier unit.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 54 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format with no declaration content.

grep -c for '"' and ';' returned 0 for 53 of the 54 files; books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp returned 62 and 1 respectively, traced line-by-line to pipe-escaped grammar-terminal symbol names, with grep -n '^;' confirming zero true comment lines.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
title: ACL2 useless-runes proof metadata retained

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

title: Repository-local audited exclusion

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
title: ACL2 useless-runes proof metadata retained

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.

Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: A zero-byte source-language file contains no declaration, theorem statement, proof, comment, identifier, or other searchable text. Excluding it from derived search indexes cannot remove mathematical content. The path remains present in the authoritative source checkout and in the filtering ledger.
title: Empty formal-source file

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
title: ACL2 useless-runes proof metadata retained

justification: A zero-byte source-language file contains no declaration, theorem statement, proof, comment, identifier, or other searchable text. Excluding it from derived search indexes cannot remove mathematical content. The path remains present in the authoritative source checkout and in the filtering ledger.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
title: ACL2 useless-runes proof metadata retained

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
title: ACL2 useless-runes proof metadata retained

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

title: Empty formal-source file

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

The superficially similar knuth-91/certify.lsp was inspected and excluded from this selector because its defpkg declarations are unique formal interface content.

justification: This file is excluded only because an accepted repository-review record targets its exact current content through an exact path, exact path set, or literal subtree prefix. The review record is pinned to the reviewed work-unit snapshot and records the repository-local rationale, content-level losslessness invariant, evidence, selector, and source provenance. FD-018 authorizes no filename, path role, generated directory, or cross-repository class by itself; any changed work-unit snapshot makes the review stale and blocks indexing until it is re-audited.
title: Repository-local audited exclusion

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

evidence.rationale: Remove exact synthetic Gate-B filesystem/hash regression fixtures while retaining actual mathematical benchmark statements and targets.
review_evidence: Complete inspection covered every Lean file under tools/gate_b/tests/fixtures in this unit.
The fixture paths themselves distinguish invalid_sha_mismatch and valid_tree test cases, while the same repository separately retains its real benchmark-goals, goals and targets surfaces.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

title: Exact-content duplicate formal source

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

evidence.rationale: This is a trust-audit script. Its only commands are `#print axioms <name>` for theorems that other indexed files declare, and scripts/audit_axioms.py parses the output. In search it only repeats theorem names already present in their owner files.

Declaration-keyword grep: 0 declarations. I read lines 1-40 and sampled every 60th line through the end.

They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
title: Parser-verified Lean import-only module retained

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
title: Parser-verified Lean import-only module retained

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
title: Parser-verified Lean import-only module retained

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
title: Parser-verified Lean import-only module retained

justification: A zero-byte source-language file contains no declaration, theorem statement, proof, comment, identifier, or other searchable text. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.

They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
title: Parser-verified Lean import-only module retained

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
